issues.description: Silent switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream changes middleware contract without explanation.
issues.detail: The example swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read() in JSONTranslator. The two are not substitutable: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length, stream does not. This change is load-bearing for the new 400 test, yet has no comment, docstring, or versionchanged note explaining why. Name the contract and document the swap.

issues.description: FAQ example is more elaborate than the lesson it teaches and obscures the actual point.
issues.detail: The lesson is how to override headers in simulate_post, but PostTest layers Content-Length checks, a conditional read, and three status codes around it. The contrived 400 path teaches the wrong mental model and includes an unbounded read of client-supplied Content-Length. Strip to the minimal handler that demonstrates header override.

issues.description: README diff bundles unrelated reformatting and semantic changes far beyond the PR's stated scope.
issues.detail: Cosmetic reflow is intertwined with real edits: StorageError.handle parameter reorder, str status to code_to_http_status, and bounded_stream swap. Three independent changes in one review prevent reviewers from separating value-bearing edits from typography. Split into separate commits, and verify the handle() signature matches Falcon's current error-handler contract.

issues.description: New tests bundle multiple independent assertions and do not name the contract under test.
issues.detail: test_things_advanced packs GET, repeat GETs, successful POST, and malformed-length POST into one function with shared state, so a resp3 failure masks resp4. No docstring states which invariant (auth, JSON, body-required) each block enforces, so a future failure cannot be distinguished from accident. Split into named tests with one-line spec comments.

issues.description: The contract for a lying Content-Length is never named, so the new test pins an accident.
issues.detail: resp4 expects 400 for empty body with Content-Length: 1, but that outcome exists only because of the unexplained bounded_stream swap. Before adding the test, state the contract: is a lying Content-Length a client error, a transport concern, or undefined? Once the contract is named, the test and code follow.

issues.description: FAQ uses `assert(...)` function-call form, a known pytest footgun in copied code.
issues.detail: `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` reads like a function call and is a classic pytest pitfall (assert on a tuple silently passes). FAQ snippets get copied verbatim, so write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400` without parentheses.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, reasonable test addition wrapped around an unexplained semantic change: req.stream becomes req.bounded_stream in the example middleware, which is load-bearing for the new 400 assertion but has no comment, docstring, or contract statement. The FAQ example is more elaborate than the header-override lesson it claims to teach and includes an unbounded read of client-supplied Content-Length that readers will copy. The README diff smuggles unrelated cosmetic reflow together with real semantic edits (handle signature reorder, status construction, bounded_stream) and should be split. Tests bundle independent cases into one function without naming the contract under test. None of this blocks merge on correctness, but the scope discipline and spec discipline are thin.
